title: Nasal [ɛ̃] — in, im, yn, ym, ain, aim, ein, eim (set 8)
focus: All of these spellings make the same nasal vowel [ɛ̃], as in « vin ». They're only nasal when the next letter is not a vowel or another n/m — compare « pain » vs « semaine », « fin » vs « fine », « plein » vs « pleine ». In Québec, [ɛ̃] is often a little closer (nearer a nasal « é »), and « un » stays a separate sound rather than merging with « in » as it does in Paris. « donne » has a double n, so it isn't nasal.

sentences.fr: Mon oncle a une ferme près de S[ain]t-Hyac[in]the.
sentences.en: My uncle has a farm near Saint-Hyacinthe.

sentences.fr: Il y a des poules, des lap[in]s et des d[in]dons.
sentences.en: There are hens, rabbits and turkeys.

sentences.fr: Le mat[in], mon oncle donne du gr[ain] aux poules.
sentences.en: In the morning, my uncle gives grain to the hens.

sentences.fr: C'est un travail [im]portant, mais il aime ça.
sentences.en: It's important work, but he likes it.
